# VELORYZ Project Creator — Documentation Library

**Maintainer:** VELORYZ Studio team · **Edition:** 2026-11-21 · **Audience:** visitors, designers, developers, studio administrators and reviewers.

This library documents the **implemented Creator V4 wizard**, its supporting services and requirements that still need operational confirmation. It is maintained in source control alongside the application. It is **not** a public terms of service, a copyright certificate, proof of deployment, or a claim that external providers are configured.

## Read these documents in order

| File | Who needs it | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [01 — Experience and navigation](./01-EXPERIENCE-AND-NAVIGATION.md) | Design, support, visitors | Screen-by-screen flow, button behavior, accessibility |
| [02 — Architecture and data flow](./02-ARCHITECTURE-AND-DATA-FLOW.md) | Developers | Browser, CMS, APIs, persistence and integration boundaries |
| [03 — Project AI operations](./03-PROJECT-AI-OPERATIONS.md) | Developers, admin, support | Provider setup, fallback behavior, troubleshooting and limits |
| [04 — Pricing and promotions](./04-PRICING-AND-PROMOTIONS.md) | Sales and admin | Estimate calculation, category settings and offer controls |
| [05 — Enquiries and portal](./05-ENQUIRIES-AND-CLIENT-PORTAL.md) | Operations and support | Reference codes, invitations, portal access and email handoff |
| [06 — Privacy and security](./06-PRIVACY-AND-SECURITY.md) | Operations, security, legal reviewer | Personal-data boundaries and controls |
| [07 — Copyright and licensing plan](./07-COPYRIGHT-AND-LICENSING.md) | Studio management, creative team, legal adviser | Ownership, external templates, licensing evidence and contract checklist |
| [08 — QA, accessibility and release](./08-QA-ACCESSIBILITY-RELEASE.md) | Developers and testers | Reproducible test cases and launch gates |
| [09 — Incident and troubleshooting](./09-TROUBLESHOOTING.md) | Support and engineering | Diagnosing broken controls, AI, email and pricing |
| [10 — Content and support copy](./10-CONTENT-AND-COMMUNICATION.md) | UX writers, sales, support | Approved claims, safe wording and messaging sequence |

## Where the implementation lives

- UI and wizard state: `public/creator-v4.js`, `public/creator-v4.css`
- Project assistant: `public/creator-ai.js`, `lib/studio-platform.mjs`, `lib/cms-api.mjs`
- Shared estimator: `public/planner-model.js`; proposal PDF: `public/creator-proposal.js`
- Main-page shell, old route and shared widgets: `lib/site-shell.ts`, `public/app.js`, `public/platform.js`
- Enquiry handling: `lib/enquiries.mjs`; admin: `public/admin.js`, `public/admin-client.js`
- Private portal: `public/client-portal.js`, `supabase/functions/veloryz-client-portal-api/index.ts`
- Tests: `tools/test-creator-v4.mjs`, `tools/test-project-ai.mjs`

## Status legend

**Implemented in source** means a code path exists and was reviewed/tested at source level. **Requires deployment verification** means only a live request or browser check can confirm operation. **Requires configuration** means credentials, host binding, email domain verification or admin setup are still necessary. **Planned** means no claim of implementation is made.

## Update procedure

When changing a feature, update the corresponding document in the same commit, adjust tests, and record any behavioral change in the pull-request or commit description. Claims of delivery or rights ownership require evidence rather than marketing language.

documents.description: One question at a time, accessibility, buttons and navigation behavior.
documents.markdown:
# 01 — Experience and navigation specification

## Product goal and boundaries

The Create page at `/create/` is a dedicated, quiet, mostly white project intake experience. Its job is to collect one clear decision at a time, produce a nonbinding estimate and structured PDF, and submit a brief for team review. It must not act like a homepage, an automatically approved quotation, or a client portal.

The primary visual inspiration is professional document-oriented software (clean white surfaces and calm typography) with one-question-per-screen pacing. This project uses original code and preview illustrations; it does not claim to reproduce third-party CSS or assets.

## Screens and sequence

1. **Welcome:** one primary **Start a project** button, official VELORYZ logo, short intro, saved-draft option when available.
2. **Discover:** select the category (e.g. business, portfolio, store, SaaS, custom app). One category selection advances.
3. **Template:** select among original VELORYZ concepts, credited external marketplace links, or **Start with a blank canvas**. The external links do not confer a template license.
4. **Style / palette:** choose visual direction and color mood. Optional custom reference URL follows.
5. **Pages and goal:** choose number of major pages/screens; describe the project outcome (minimum ten characters).
6. **Conditional capabilities:** Content, Experience, Commerce, Operations and App feature groups appear according to category. Some selected features trigger one additional scoping question.
7. **Existing materials:** select brand kit, text, images or existing site; skippable.
8. **Budget:** pick a budget preference, see category-aware planning ranges and transparent assumptions. App budgets can be higher than simple-site budgets.
9. **Timeline / priorities:** preferred launch window and tradeoff (speed, craft, lean first release, balance).
10. **Contact:** name, valid email, consent.
11. **Review:** editable answers, early price range, discussion links, proposed PDF and Send button.
12. **Success:** only after the server confirms the request; show the server-issued reference and the separate later invitation workflow.

The number of screens varies with category and selected capabilities. Do not promise a fixed question count.

## Navigation contract

- On every question, the **top sticky bar** contains Back and Continue (or **Send my project** on Review). There is **no bottom Continue bar**.
- The same tab URL changes using `?question=<step>`; URL Back and Forward should restore the corresponding question.
- Pressing Enter advances from appropriate text fields, but never intercepts multiline text input or marketplace search.
- The final Review has **Edit** shortcuts. After editing, a **Review** shortcut returns without replaying all questions.
- Validation failures remain in the current question and show a visible error; no silent skipping.
- A request may only display the success panel when the server responds successfully. Never generate a fake reference or access code in the browser.
- The browser tab stores draft progress in `sessionStorage`; successful submission removes the saved draft. This is not cross-device synchronization.

## Layout and isolation

`public/app.js` marks the creator route with `body.v4-creator-page` and avoids mounting older site chat and campaign widgets there. `public/creator-v4.css` hides the original site header/footer and legacy guided-project elements **only on the Create route while the wizard is mounted**. The homepage 3D V structures and Playground are not modified.

The VELORYZ Project AI launcher is at the **bottom-left corner**, separate from top navigation, with a visible open/close state and keyboard focus. It is accessible from the welcome screen and steps. The AI panel is an optional helper; if the AI is unavailable, the core creator must remain usable.

## Responsive and accessible behavior

- The top action bar becomes two rows on small screens; Back and Continue remain visible.
- Prevent the sticky header from entirely obscuring focused elements, as covered by WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.11: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum
- Use visible focus styles, readable label+input relationships, `role=alert` for errors, and progressive keyboard navigation.
- Respect reduced-motion preferences. Avoid scroll hijacking and overlay competition with mobile keyboards.
- Test touch targets, long descriptions, zoom at 200%/400%, narrow widths, viewport changes and assistive technologies.

## Acceptance criteria

A new visitor can choose a category, continue, navigate back, resume a tab draft, modify features, change price preference, download the proposal, and submit using the server API. The old “Create your project” panel must not appear beneath this wizard. The AI button must open from the left without blocking top navigation.

# 02 — Technical architecture and data-flow map

## Source layout and loading

`lib/site-shell.ts` serves the public HTML shell. The relevant script order is:

1. `public/planner-model.js` — shared normalization and estimate functions.
2. `public/platform.js` — legacy public catalogue and original Create-page function.
3. `public/creator-proposal.js` — local PDF generation.
4. `public/creator-v4.js` — overrides the Create-page renderer and exposes `window.VeloryzCreatorV4`.
5. `public/app.js` — site-wide SPA route rendering.
6. `public/creator-ai.js` — independent project-AI widget and event handlers.

This dependency order matters: loading the new creator before the shared planner or leaving its script cached can result in the older Create page appearing.

The Create route stays in the public site SPA, but it is visually and behaviorally isolated. `public/app.js` adds `v4-creator-page` to the body, skips global expert/campaign widgets on that route, and does not re-render an active wizard merely because the CMS version changed. The creator uses a scoped event handler that prevents the site's legacy click listeners from swallowing button actions.

## Runtime state and data ownership

| Data | Source | Lifetime / owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Category, template, features, goal, budget, contact | `creator-v4.js` state | Browser session draft; user can edit |
| Base and category allowances, promotion metadata | Published CMS `state.site.creatorPricing` | Team-managed, from `/api/site`; code defaults are fallback |
| Planning low/high | `VeloryzPlanner.estimate()` | Recomputed in browser; not binding |
| Project PDF | `VeloryzProposal.build/download()` | Browser-generated file, not automatically submitted |
| Project enquiry | `POST /api/enquiries` | Server-held private inbox, once accepted |
| Project reference | Enquiry API response | Issued by server, shown after success |
| Client invitation token | Private portal admin API | Separately created after workspace setup, one-time use |
| AI messages | `creator-ai.js` in-memory store | Page instance; client sends limited project context to AI API |

## HTTP boundaries

### `POST /api/enquiries`

Accepts a project request with a UUID request ID, name, valid email, nontrivial message, budget preference and consent. The server validates length, origin, rate/fingerprint and database insert. On success returns a reference. See `lib/enquiries.mjs` for authoritative validation logic. A network error does not prove submission failed; safe retries use the same request ID.

### `POST /api/project-ai`

The independent server endpoint is in `lib/cms-api.mjs` and dispatches to `projectCreatorAi()` in `lib/studio-platform.mjs`. It validates a bounded alternating user/assistant conversation and project context, checks configured AI provider / Workers binding, and rate limits requests. It does not issue token, payment or quote actions. Actual availability depends on runtime credentials/bindings.

### `GET /api/site`

Returns the published CMS state. The browser uses `site.creatorPricing` for public planning estimates and the optional, approved promotion. Updates in Studio Control require saving and publishing; an existing quote does not silently change.

### `/api/client-portal/*`

A separate private backend handles admin project creation, invitations, token redemption and client messages. Its storage and authorization are not the same as the public project enquiry form.

## Failure boundaries and graceful degradation

- No project-AI model: optional helper shows clearly labeled *prewritten guide* suggestions; no fabricated live-model output.
- No CMS response: page uses the last published or code fallback where available; do not misstate live prices as an approved quote.
- No enquiry DB: submission fails visibly, draft retained, provide contact alternatives.
- No email provider: invite can require manual owner delivery; never show “email sent” without provider evidence.
- Old scripts cached: bust the creator JS/CSS versions in `site-shell.ts`, reload and test.

## Change-impact checklist

Changes to `creator-v4.js` should update `test-creator-v4.mjs`; changes to AI must update `test-project-ai.mjs`; server API changes require validation/negative-path tests; pricing changes require CMS validation + estimate tests; navigation changes require browser Back/Forward and mobile keyboard tests.

documents.markdown:
# 03 — Dedicated VELORYZ Project AI: operation and support

## Intent and identity

VELORYZ Project AI is a **project-scoping assistant**, not Nikhil, Happy or another persona bot. It helps with requirements, feature selection, budgets, milestones, MVP phasing and questions about post-submission access. It is advisory only; it cannot approve contracts, discounts, deliverables or client invitations.

**Client widget:** `public/creator-ai.js`.
**Route:** `POST /api/project-ai` in `lib/cms-api.mjs`.
**Server implementation:** `projectCreatorAi()` in `lib/studio-platform.mjs`, using `resolveAiSettings()` and model-provider request logic.

## Production activation

1. Deploy the latest code containing the route and the JS/CSS. The frontend button and the endpoint must be deployed together.
2. Choose a live provider in **Studio Control → AI settings**, or provide a production Worker AI binding. Provider credentials stay server-side. For OpenAI/Gemini, follow the existing server configuration; never place keys in browser code, GitHub markdown, HTML or screenshots.
3. Verify the provider actually responds to a bounded question on the production host. A configured key, build success or AI icon is **not** evidence of live inference.
4. Confirm the response has `available:true`, `mode:'ai'` and a meaningful `answer`; check provider billing/quota and permitted models.
5. Test both direct visit `/create/` and SPA navigation into Create from another site page.

The project AI backend attempts the configured provider; if that fails and the Cloudflare Workers `AI` binding is available, it attempts the configured Workers model. If neither is operational, the API returns **503**, `PROJECT_AI_UNAVAILABLE` (or a specific validation/rate error).

## Non-AI fallback

The client includes **prewritten studio guidance** for common project questions. When the live endpoint cannot respond, the widget labels the material `STUDIO GUIDE · PREWRITTEN`, and says the live AI is unavailable. This fallback is not a generative answer, not proof that the model is connected, and cannot issue a quotation or client code. Visitors may keep using the creator or contact the team.

## Data minimization and restrictions

The client sends message text, stage, category, visual style, budget preference, project goal and feature names. It does not intentionally include the visitor's dedicated email field. Visitors can nevertheless enter personal information in free-text goals or messages; warn them not to submit secrets. The server limits message count/size, applies origin checks and rate limits. Its system instructions forbid secrets, impersonation and fictional pricing commitments.

Live-model outputs are informational and may contain errors; the final brief, scope, quote and invitation must be reviewed by the team.

## Troubleshooting decision tree

1. **No launcher**: check creator script order, `creator-ai.js` response status, client console, `studio:route` event and presence of `#v4-ai-slot`.
2. **Launcher visible but cannot click**: inspect overlays, pointer-events, z-index, stale CSS, capture/bubble event conflicts, and left-screen position.
3. **Panel opens, send fails**: inspect Network → `POST /api/project-ai`; log HTTP status and server request ID if provided. Do not send passwords to support.
4. **HTTP 503**: check binding, provider health, billing, API key permissions and model name in protected config; test from production runtime.
5. **HTTP 429**: existing rate limit is operating. Do not disable limits to fix an overloaded client.
6. **HTTP 4xx validation**: review bounded conversation shape and message lengths; client must send alternating user/assistant roles.
7. **Only prewritten guidance**: a useful fallback exists, but the live provider is not functioning. Confirm the exact provider path before advertising “live AI”.

## Verification checklist

- Opens and closes on desktop/mobile from the bottom-left.
- Supports mouse, touch and keyboard.
- A valid live-provider test produces an actual provider reply.
- No provider yields visible offline status and correctly labeled guide.
- Messages are not sent to unrelated persona chats.
- No personal client email or access code is automatically injected into prompt context.
- Long, malformed and repeated requests fail safely; core wizard stays usable.

documents.description: Pricing assumptions, consultation, offers and quote approvals.
documents.markdown:
# 04 — Pricing model, offers and quotation governance

## Principle

The wizard produces an **illustrative planning range**, not a quote or payment request. The user's budget preference is not necessarily the amount the studio will charge. Price depends on real requirements, integrations, security, design depth, testing, revision limits, recurring services, third-party licenses and the final contract.

## Implemented calculator

`public/planner-model.js` normalizes the selected project and computes a base allowance, additional-page allowance, selected-feature allowances and a high-range contingency. A category-specific base differentiates simple sites from Ecommerce, SaaS and Custom App work. Complex technical features widen the high range. Values are **planning assumptions** maintained in code/CMS, not externally verified competitors' prices.

Published data comes from `site.creatorPricing`; `lib/cms-api.mjs` validates it before publishing and merges defaults for legacy published states. The UI recalculates after relevant project changes. It does not silently substitute the visitor's budget as the offer price.

## Team-editable controls

In Studio Control → Settings:

- Starting allowance for non-specialized/simple cases.
- Allowance per extra page beyond four.
- Standard feature allowance.
- Upper planning contingency percentage.
- Category starting allowances for Business, Portfolio, Agency, Ecommerce, Restaurant, Editorial, Education, Community, SaaS/platform and Custom App.

**Operations:** review actual time/cost data, adjust a *draft*, have a second person review category pricing, publish the change, then test a business brief, a shop brief and a custom-app brief. Verify displayed figures on `/create/`. Maintain a dated internal pricing decisions log.

## Larger budgets

The creator accepts preferences up to ₹15 lakh for platforms/custom apps, with smaller maxima for simple websites and intermediate limits for stores. These are selection bounds, **not** maximum studio prices.

## Published promotions

The team can optionally publish a creator promotion with: enabled toggle, title, eligibility/terms, optional promo code, advertised percentage and expiration. It is **disabled by default**. Terms must be specific and truthful; never advertise invented savings.

A visible promotion is not automatically applied to the calculator. A visitor may request offer review with their enquiry. The studio must determine eligibility, dates, exclusions, stackability and the written quote. A code in a public offer is a **marketing code** and is never a client portal secret.

## Offers and consumer-friendly copy

Allowed: “Ask our team about a leaner first release,” “Scope can be phased,” “A current offer may be available subject to terms,” “Prices are estimates until the team confirms scope.”

Avoid: “Guaranteed lowest price,” “Only today” without real expiry, “Automatic 40% off” without valid approved terms, “Your final price is ₹X,” “Every estimate can be reduced,” or fabricated comparison to competitors.

The final written proposal should itemize development, design, add-ons, applicable tax, support, hosting, third-party licenses, payment timing, revisions and acceptance conditions.

## Commercial review checklist

Confirm the requirements, screen count and roles; price custom integrations separately; specify accessibility and security deliverables; document assumptions, exclusions, changes and quote validity; record any discount approver and offer ID; secure client acceptance through the agreed process. A PDF downloaded from Create is **not** evidence of binding acceptance.

documents.markdown:
# 05 — Enquiry submission, reference numbers and client invitation

## Important: two unrelated codes

1. **Project reference:** the enquiry service returns a code like `VZ-...` after a successful request. It identifies an enquiry for support and is **not a password**, credential or activation token.
2. **Client invitation / activation code:** a cryptographically generated, one-time secret created by an authorized team administrator **after** the team creates or approves a private client workspace. It is used at `/client/`.

A project request must never automatically create an invitation or display a fake token. A reference code is not accepted as a portal login code.

## Visitor journey

1. Complete the question-by-question brief and enter a **required email**.
2. Give explicit contact-data consent.
3. Click the top **Send my project** action at the review screen. The browser sends `POST /api/enquiries` with a UUID request ID and structured summary.
4. Wait for an actual successful HTTP response. Show **Project submitted successfully** and the real `reference` from the server.
5. Give the visitor clear next steps: save the reference, check inbox/spam, allow team review, receive a later separate invitation if workspace created, open `/client/` and redeem it.

The suggested “check email within 12 hours” is a **check-in suggestion**, not a guaranteed response, token or email delivery SLA.

## Server behavior

`lib/enquiries.mjs` validates required fields, consent, JSON shape, maximum message length and request id. It uses database fingerprints for safe retries and applies source-based rate limits. It persists an entry in the private enquiry store and returns an actual reference on success. Invalid or unavailable requests must show a visible error; keep draft data for retry.

## Team management procedure

1. In Studio Control → Project console, open the new enquiry and review the requested project and email.
2. Mark status / add a response note according to the team's internal process. New requests older than 12 hours are flagged as needing follow-up; this is a reminder, not proof of contact.
3. If appropriate, create a private client project using the enquiry's contact and scope, then add status, phase, next step, milestones, deliverable links, approvals and messages.
4. Generate an invitation through the **private** portal admin operation. Do not create it in browser JavaScript or manually invent a “secret code.”
5. Inspect delivery status. The provider can accept, fail or be unavailable. If configured but delivery fails, follow the explicitly supported manual process.
6. Instruct the client to enter the actual invitation at `https://veloryz.online/client/`. Never ask them to send the secret to unrelated chats or public support threads.

## Invitation mechanics — current private backend

The private edge-function code and existing `CLIENT-PORTAL-WORKFLOW.md` specify 128-bit random invite material, server-side hash storage, a 14-day invitation expiry, one-time redemption and a 7-day secure session cookie. The client can then see only its project. Generating a replacement invitation revokes previous invitations/sessions for that project.

Email is attempted through **Resend** only when `RESEND_API_KEY` and `PORTAL_FROM_EMAIL` are configured in the private edge-function environment. Sender identity must be verified. A provider “accepted” response does not guarantee arrival in the inbox.

## Support scripts

**Request confirmation:** “Your project request has been received. Save the reference shown on screen; our team will review the scope and contact you using the email in your brief.”

**Portal explanation:** “The project reference is not the access code. A separate private invitation is issued after your workspace is set up. When you receive it, open /client/ and redeem the one-time code.”

**If code not received:** “Check the entered email and spam folder. Please share your *reference number*, not a private invitation token, so our team can locate the enquiry.”

## Things not implemented automatically

No immediate access token on submission, no guaranteed 12-hour email delivery, no automatic project acceptance, no automatic legal agreement, no payment charge and no automatic quote approval.

documents.description: How client information is handled, security controls and open tasks.
documents.markdown:
# 06 — Privacy, security and data-handling plan

**Status:** mixture of implemented controls and operational requirements. This document does **not** certify compliance with any specific privacy law or security standard. Team review with a qualified privacy/legal specialist is required before public policy claims.

## Data collected

The browser collects project category, style, features, goals, budget preference, materials and optional inspiration link. On submission it collects name and email, with explicit consent. The project enquiry server stores the submitted brief and contact data. The Project AI gets limited project context and user questions; the client code intentionally excludes the dedicated email field.

Note: a visitor could still type their email or secrets into a goal or chat question. The UI should advise against sharing passwords, API keys or confidential customer data with AI.

## Data flow and access controls

| Location | Data | Access / safeguards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Session storage | In-progress brief, possibly name/email | Local tab/browser; cleared on successful submission |
| Public enquiry endpoint | Project brief and contact information | Validation, same-origin checks, consent, rate limiting, private storage |
| Admin console | Enquiry and client project | Authenticated studio admins; do not leak via frontend public state |
| Private portal backend | Client projects, invitation hashes, sessions, messages | Project-scoped access checks and secure cookie session |
| AI inference provider | Questions plus project context | Server-side credentials, bounded input, no intentional email-field forwarding |
| External template/WhatsApp/email links | Outbound navigation | Clearly labeled external service, provider privacy terms apply |

## Implemented constraints to preserve

- Credentials and service-role secrets never enter public JS or documentation.
- Enquiry requests have bounded JSON fields, consent, validation and server-side reference creation.
- One-time client invitations store hashes rather than plaintext in the private database.
- Private portal sessions use secure, HttpOnly cookie settings according to the current backend.
- AI input is bounded and rate limited. The optional AI cannot approve payment or issue tokens.
- Template links open external sites with safe navigation attributes.

## Privacy work to complete before production claims

1. Publish an accurate privacy notice naming the data controller/contact address, collection purposes, retention rules, third-party processors and user request process.
2. Set written retention/deletion periods for rejected enquiries, approved projects, AI logs, portal messages and uploaded media. **No automatic retention policy is asserted here**.
3. Review lawful bases, children's data, cross-border transfers and processor contracts appropriate to the jurisdictions served.
4. Verify no access-code values are written to logs, analytics, client storage or URL tracking parameters.
5. Audit admin access and incident-response permissions; ensure staff can revoke credentials and sessions.
6. Test SQL/RPC authorization and RLS; do not assume private data is secure based only on the frontend.
7. Confirm backup, restore, deletion and data export procedures before making public commitments.

## Incident response basics

If a secret/token is leaked: revoke or regenerate it through the supported admin workflow, check logs, notify authorized staff, and assess notification obligations. If a client can view another project: disable access, isolate the faulty authorization rule, gather evidence without exposing more data and do not restore access until verified.

documents.markdown:
# 07 — Copyright, design ownership and third-party licensing plan

**Purpose:** a practical rights checklist for VELORYZ projects, template inspirations, source code, fonts, media, branding and deliverables. **This is a planning document, not legal advice or a signed agreement.** Have qualified counsel adapt contracts and verify the applicable jurisdiction.

## Rights principles

1. **Original work:** record who actually created code, UI layouts, illustrations, logos, product copy and media. Employment/commission terms affect rights. A file in the repository is not, by itself, a complete chain-of-title record.
2. **External reference ≠ license:** Framer, Webflow, Mobbin, Bonsai, Dubsado and marketplace listings may inspire general visual direction. Do not copy distinctive layouts, CSS, source files, images, fonts, screenshots, logos or a paid template without an appropriate license.
3. **Client-provided material:** require the client to confirm they have rights or permissions to use submitted logos, photographs, brand copy, music, datasets, testimonials and trademarks.
4. **Third-party dependencies:** preserve applicable OSS notices and license files. Check each font, asset, icon, animation library, package and template under its own terms, including attribution and redistribution.
5. **Ownership transfer:** do not promise “full ownership” solely because a deposit or quote is paid. Define transferred rights and retained rights in a signed statement/contract; consider pre-existing tools and third-party licenses separately.
6. **AI-generated output:** do not assume generated content is exclusive, noninfringing or protectable. Review outputs for similarity, identifiable brands, permissions and provider terms before commercial use.

## Source files requiring evidence review

| Asset/component | Current observation | Required action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Official VELORYZ logo & wordmark | Files under `public/assets/brand/official/` | Verify studio authorship/assignment and any underlying stock elements; keep provenance record |
| Handcrafted homepage/Playground 3D V structures | Existing source/models and `public/assets/brand/` | Preserve unmodified per product brief; document author, source mesh and licensed textures |
| 12 original Creator visual concepts | CSS previews / preset data in `creator-v4.js` | Confirm original implementation; do not claim they are third-party licensed templates |
| 26 marketplace inspiration links | Named, credited external URLs in template library | Link to originals, disclose references are not purchased/installed; revisit broken links |
| Fonts | `public/assets/font-license.txt` | Audit exact families, formats and weight usage; retain notices and any distribution limits |
| 3D and frontend libraries | `public/assets/brand/THREE-LICENSE.txt`, package dependencies | Run license audit and preserve required notices |
| Design preview media | `public/assets/designs/` (including license folder) | Record author, license URL, purchase receipt, restrictions and expiration where relevant |
| User-supplied media | Collected during production projects | Obtain rights warranty or actual license; use only for agreed purpose |
| Third-party branding/screenshots | External URLs and product examples | Avoid uploading unchanged third-party screenshots into template previews without permission |

## Copyright / contract checklist (to adapt with counsel)

Include in each client agreement:
- Parties, project identity, deliverables and acceptance criteria.
- Exactly which intellectual-property rights are assigned or licensed; exclusive/nonexclusive scope, territories, duration, permitted uses, changes and sublicensing.
- Whether assignment is conditional on full payment and which pre-existing libraries, internal methods and reusable components remain with the studio.
- Terms for source-code handoff, hosting access, credentials, domain names and repositories.
- Third-party components: license responsibility, fees, attribution, availability, renewals and restrictions.
- Client warranties for supplied assets and consequences of infringement claims.
- Portfolio/showcase permissions, confidentiality, privacy and publicity rights.
- Revision/change requests, termination, refunds, maintenance and disputed deliverables.
- AI-assisted content review and human approval before publication.
- Signed instrument requirements and record retention.

**India-specific note:** Sections 17–19 of the Indian Copyright Act, 1957 address first ownership, assignment and the mode/form of assignment. In particular, do not rely on an informal “all rights included” line where a properly documented transfer is needed. Consult the statute and a lawyer for applicability:
- Official IP India statute overview: https://ipindia.gov.in/acts/copyright-act-1957
- Assignment of copyright (Section 18): https://ipindia.gov.in/acts/copyright-act-1957/section-18-4
- Mode of assignment (Section 19): https://ipindia.gov.in/acts/copyright-act-1957/section-19-2

## Asset-rights register template (internal)

For each asset, track: `asset_id | project | filename/URL | creator/owner | acquired_on | source | license_type | license_text_or_receipt | attribution | redistribution_allowed | commercial_use_allowed | derivative_allowed | expiry | reviewer | status`.

Status should be **Unverified**, **Cleared**, **Restricted** or **Blocked**. Only use or publish assets marked **Cleared** after evidence review. Do not invent missing license approvals. Keep the register in an access-controlled team location; store purchase receipts separately from the public repo.

## External design-reference rules

Use title and original link for discovery; write original descriptions; never pass off a concept sketch as a screenshot of the linked product; never claim a marketplace license is included by choosing it in the wizard. If a client wants an actual marketplace template, purchase or obtain the proper license and document the approved usage before importing it.

## Suggested public-facing clause for legal review

“Third-party templates, fonts, photography, plugins and other licensed components are subject to their respective rights and fees. The studio will identify any material third-party dependencies and the rights granted to the client in the project agreement.”

This is draft language requiring legal approval; it is not automatically part of the website's terms.

documents.markdown:
# 08 — QA plan, accessibility requirements and release gates

## Automated commands

From `VELORYZ-Studio/`:

```sh
npm run test:creator
npm run test:project-ai
npm run test:all
npm run build
```

These checks require a compatible Node version and installed project dependencies; do not interpret a source syntax check as a passing production build.

## Functional regression matrix

| ID | Scenario | Required result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NAV-01 | Open /create/ directly | Welcome screen only, no original guided project panel below |
| NAV-02 | Click Start a project | Discover question opens in same tab |
| NAV-03 | On each question click **top Continue** | One screen advances, never a hidden bottom button |
| NAV-04 | Click top Back | Previous question restored without data loss |
| NAV-05 | Browser Back/Forward | URL and screen remain in sync |
| NAV-06 | Return from Review/Edit | Changed answer persists and Review shortcut works |
| NAV-07 | Enter a malformed email | Inline validation, no request submitted |
| NAV-08 | Submit with valid consent | Actual POST succeeds, server reference shown |
| NAV-09 | API fails/timeout | Visible error; draft preserved and safe retry possible |
| NAV-10 | Completed request | Draft cleared, reference remains visible on confirmation |
| LIB-01 | Open studio template library | 12 concepts and category/search controls present |
| LIB-02 | Open external reference | Original credited URL opens without granting a license |
| COST-01 | Business versus app budget | Distinct category baselines, clear nonbinding language |
| COST-02 | Published promotion | Accurate eligibility/expiry, opt-in only, no auto deduction |
| AI-01 | Widget on Welcome | Button visible at bottom-left and opens |
| AI-02 | Wizard route transition | Panel remounts after navigation; chat history retained in page memory |
| AI-03 | Working model | Verified live answer from the intended provider, not another persona |
| AI-04 | No model/503 | Honest offline status and labeled prewritten guidance |
| AI-05 | Contact-data boundary | Email input not automatically included in AI context |
| PORTAL-01 | Confirmation copy | Reference distinguished from separate invitation |
| PORTAL-02 | 12-hour copy | No guaranteed 12-hour delivery or immediate token |
| PORTAL-03 | Visit /client/ | Portal expects a real team-issued invite, not project reference |
| ISO-01 | Create route | Legacy expert launcher, old planner, footer and offer widgets hidden |
| ISO-02 | Exit Create | Other routes still show their original navigation/widgets as intended |

## Browser/device matrix

Desktop: recent Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari where supported. Mobile: iOS Safari and Android Chrome; test portrait and landscape, virtual keyboard open, 320/375/430 px widths, touch hit areas, 200% and 400% zoom. Test keyboard-only navigation and a screen reader on at least one desktop/mobile setup.

## Accessibility review

Target WCAG 2.2 AA where applicable. Examine:
- SC 2.4.11: focused elements not entirely obscured by sticky top bar — https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum
- Focus visibility; contrast; logical tab order; name/role/value; form errors and assistance; landmark structure; reduced motion; accessible dialog/panel behavior.
- AI messages have a live log and their provenance labeled; do not move keyboard focus unexpectedly on rerender.
- No icon-only button without a meaningful accessible name.

## Release gate

**Ready to deploy** only when code review and automated tests pass, asset version hashes are refreshed, release notes list changes and rollback target is recorded.

**Ready to declare live** only after checking the deployed `/create/` HTML, stylesheet and scripts, visiting in a real browser, completing a test enquiry against real backend, checking Project AI provider availability, and confirming no legacy content below the wizard.

**Ready to promise email delivery** only after a real test invitation shows accepted provider status **and** recipient inbox receipt for a verified sending domain. Even then, do not guarantee a specific time without operational capacity and monitoring.

## What was and was not verified at code authoring

Source syntax, markup assertions and simulated journeys may pass without proving hosting has deployed. A test stub returning `{reference:'VZ-EXAMPLE-123'}` is not an actual production enquiry. Model-binding stubs are not live AI evidence. Record real browser screenshots/results in a release checklist before changing these statuses.

documents.markdown:
# 09 — Support and incident troubleshooting runbook

## Symptom: Continue/Start is unresponsive

1. Check the actual deployed `creator-v4.js` version and browser console errors.
2. Confirm the DOM includes `.v4-root` and the clicked control has `data-v4-action`.
3. Verify `/create/` has the `v4-creator-page` body class.
4. Confirm legacy click handlers are not canceling events; creator controls use a scoped capturing click handler with default prevention and propagation isolation.
5. Check form validation. Missing goal/name/email/consent should display an inline message rather than silently advance.
6. Test mouse, touch and keyboard. Retest on an incognito browser to eliminate stale cache.
7. Check whether a CMS refresh or SPA navigation is unexpectedly replacing `#main`; the current creator must not be wiped during form entry.

## Symptom: Old Create your project visible under the wizard

- Inspect `#main` children and the active route; the page should contain only the mounted Creator V4 root for the creator view.
- Verify `body.v4-creator-page` CSS loaded and the creator's stylesheet has the newest version.
- Check `public/platform.js` old `createPage()` and any late-injected planner widgets.
- A stale script order can cause the older route renderer to win. See [Architecture](./02-ARCHITECTURE-AND-DATA-FLOW.md).
- Do not delete the old planner source blindly: other pages may still depend on it. Isolate it by route.

## Symptom: Project AI button missing or unresponsive

- Confirm `creator-ai.js` was served, has no syntax errors, and `#v4-ai-slot` exists.
- It should mount at initial DOM ready, `studio:route`, or `veloryz:creator-render`.
- Examine overlay/z-index/pointer-events and left positioning on narrow screens.
- If panel opens but replies fail, inspect the POST to `/api/project-ai`; distinguish a frontend event problem from an unavailable inference provider.
- When provider unavailable, the client should show explicitly **prewritten** guidance, not an invented model reply.

## Symptom: The wrong pricing or an unavailable promotion appears

- Check published `site.creatorPricing`, not just admin draft.
- Verify that category-specific amounts are numbers and that the current backend recognizes the category/pricing schema.
- Check whether the promotion is enabled, terms complete and expiry current.
- Confirm an offer is not being subtracted from the automatic estimate. Recompute in a new browser session if necessary.

## Symptom: Enquiry reference missing

- Check browser Network response from `POST /api/enquiries`. A 2xx with `reference` is required for success.
- If 503, inspect the private database/backend, not the UI alone.
- Preserve the request UUID for retries; do not generate multiple unrelated references after a timeout unless necessary.
- If the server accepted a request but browser lost the response, ask the team to check the private inbox.

## Symptom: Activation email not delivered

- First confirm the team actually created a private client workspace and generated an invitation.
- Check backend delivery status (accepted/manual/failed). Confirm `RESEND_API_KEY`, verified `PORTAL_FROM_EMAIL`, sender DNS records and recipient.
- Never show the client the API key or token hash.
- Distinguish project reference from invitation code.
- Do not promise delivery in twelve hours; escalate internally if a new enquiry remains untouched.

## Incident severity examples

**P1:** cross-project data leak, unauthorized portal access, leaked provider key, payment/security issue — immediately disable affected access and escalate.
**P2:** no one can submit a project / production endpoint down / all creator controls blocked — prioritize restore or rollback and display a safe contact alternative.
**P3:** Project AI offline while creator is functional, noncritical layout issue — use labeled prewritten guidance and investigate provider/UX.
**P4:** editorial typo, broken inspiration reference or documentation inconsistency — log, assign, fix in normal release.

## Evidence to record

Timestamp, URL+query (without private tokens), browser version, screenshot with PII redacted, request status and error code, deployed commit SHA, reproduction steps, affected users (anonymized), mitigation and follow-up owner. Do not paste customer emails, private invite codes, production keys or full AI chat transcripts into public issues.

documents.markdown:
# 10 — User-facing copy, promises and team communication

## Voice

VELORYZ should sound like a capable multidisciplinary **team**: calm, direct, warm and precise. Avoid wording that makes one named person the point of contact or decision maker inside the public creator. Do not mislead visitors by claiming a large staff, available human chat, instant approval or 24/7 monitoring when those facts have not been verified.

## Standard copy for the creator

- Welcome: “Tell us what you have in mind. One thoughtful question at a time.”
- Top action: “Continue →”; Review action: “Send my project →”.
- Budget: “Early planning range”; “Your preferred budget”; “The team will confirm scope, deliverables and a written quotation.”
- Marketing: “We can discuss a smaller first release, phased delivery or eligible published offers.” Not “Guaranteed reduction.”
- AI: “Ask VELORYZ Project AI”. Live provider replies labeled “Project AI · Live model”. Model failures labeled “Studio guide · Prewritten”.
- Review: “Your project outline”; explain that the PDF is an illustrative planning document.
- Success: “Project submitted successfully”; show the exact server-generated reference.
- Email: “Check your inbox and spam folder for updates. The team may contact you; the twelve-hour window is not a guaranteed response time.”
- Portal: “A separate one-time invitation may be sent after your private project workspace is created. Enter that code at /client/.”

## Do not say

- “Your client activation code has been emailed” merely because an enquiry was submitted.
- “Your project has been approved,” “Price locked,” “Offer automatically applied,” or “AI has confirmed your quote.”
- “We always reply within 12 hours” unless the business has a verifiable service commitment.
- “We built the external marketplace template,” “Template license included,” or “Identical CSS” if only an inspiration link is provided.
- “All copyrights transferred” without a signed agreement and rights assessment.

## Team support handoff

For support by WhatsApp/email, ask for the public **project reference**, not an invitation token, password, CVV, payment credentials or customer data. Explain that contact buttons open the visitor's communication app and do not send a message automatically. Confirm the preferred communication channel only after the visitor submits it.

## Content-release checklist

Every published offer must include title, eligible audience, conditions, relevant dates, exclusion details and reviewer approval. Every external template should retain an original source link. Every privacy or ownership statement must be reviewed for factual/legal accuracy. Update UI text, documentation and tests together when these promises change.
